originality.rationale: The cited September 2026 paper proves the surface gluing and total dimension but does not give an equivariant finite symplectic character or subgroup spectrum. The 2025 predecessor proves a top-weight dimension and orientation formalism, not the current finite-group formula. Hoffman--Weintraub compute ordinary cohomology of the geometric Igusa boundary, a distinct invariant: its top-homology permutation representation cannot have the strictly negative involution trace established here. Focused indexed-publication searches found no exact equivalent. An incomplete comparison with Oda--Schwermer 1990 and possible implicit older derivations are documented as residual risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Oda--Schwermer (1990) was not available for decisive full-paper comparison; an implicit equivalent character computation there is possible.
An older representation-theoretic interpretation of Siegel boundary weight pieces may imply the signed induced module even without using tropical terminology.
Non-equivariant structural theorems provide essential input; novelty is limited to their genuine finite-group equivariant refinement and should not be exaggerated.

value.rationale: Top-weight cohomology of full-level abelian-surface moduli naturally carries a symplectic level-change action; its known dimension alone hides a negative trace for rank-two symplectic involutions and a nontrivial cyclotomic multiplicity spectrum for transvections. This gives a uniform induced representation and exact subgroup invariant dimensions across all odd primes, informing intermediate level quotient cohomology. The added character theory is structurally distinct from the already known additive Betti count and from ordinary boundary homology.
